description: server.js's own route table shows the authorization middleware for this exact route commented out: '// app.put(\'/api/Products/:id\', security.isAuthorized()) // vuln-code-snippet vuln-line changeProductChallenge'. No authentication of any kind is required to overwrite any product's name, description, or price, public, store-wide content any visitor sees, not a per-account setting like pt13's username field.
expected_exploit_indicator: A PUT request with no Authorization header at all succeeds, HTTP 200, and the product's description is actually changed when read back afterward
legitimate_check: A real admin-authenticated PUT must keep working in every condition.
test_hygiene_note: This item mutates live product data on the shared container; scenario.py restores the original description immediately after confirming the tamper, every run.
